hypothesis: The high-MOI Jurkat same-target effect contains enough target-specific landmark information to route convex weights among Experiment 132's already-allowed source-context vectors, without directly contributing any expression value to the prediction.

distinctness.experiment_107: No fixed fraction or direct Jurkat source residual is added.
distinctness.experiment_137: No chord, tangent, angular cap or source-vector interpolation is used.
distinctness.experiment_132: The exact same-target source vectors are retained; only their convex weights change.
distinctness.target_kernel_family: No other target, neighbour, embedding or target-feature response prediction is used.

parent_132.allowed_sources_per_held_group: all six source contexts except the held biological group, exactly five vectors
parent_132.comparator: equal arithmetic mean of those exact five raw uncentered same-target source vectors

jurkat_landmarks.use: cosine similarities for donor routing only

candidate_family.softmax: stable rowwise softmax of five landmark cosines divided by temperature
candidate_family.tie_break: identity, then smaller rho, then larger temperature
candidate_family.fallback: bit-exact identity for absent, nontransferable, fewer-than-16-nonzero-landmark, nonfinite or zero-norm landmark rows

development.fold_definition: contiguous numpy.array_split blocks preserving Experiment 132 target order
development.nested_selection: select on inner queries against an inner-only PDS gallery, then evaluate held queries against the complete 613-target gallery

nulls.target_label: derange high-MOI landmark rows among transferable targets and repeat complete nested selection
nulls.landmark_coordinate: derange the 138 high-MOI landmark coordinates relative to the fixed source landmark coordinates and repeat complete nested selection

bootstrap.blocks: connected components of reciprocal five-nearest DepMap neighbours at cosine >= 0.40
